title: Algorithm Atlas
subtitle: A study map for patterns, practice, and recall.
legend: • ★ LC …: a Top Interview 150 problem assigned to this branch as its main study home.
• ↔ LC …: an alternative approach or cross-reference to a problem assigned elsewhere.
• ○: a complementary branch with no primary Top 150 assignment here. It may still be a foundation used by those problems.
• OK / OK(date): your original completion marker, preserved at its original scope.
• [LATER]: your original postponement marker, even when the branch contains a Top 150 problem.
• No progress marker: progress unspecified. It does not mean “not learned.”
Dates are DD-MM-YYYY. A parent's OK does not automatically mark newly added children or individual problems as solved. Problem assignments are a study organization, not exclusive labels.
overview: Array and strings — your original parent taxonomy
├── Sliding Window Note: a specialized use of two pointers; kept as its own family.
├── Prefix Sum Extended below with related Prefix / Suffix aggregates.
sourceNotes: All original OK markers, dates, review reminders, [LATER] tags, concepts and learning notes are retained. Obvious spelling and formatting issues were cleaned up. No additional completed status was inferred.
Three technical clarifications were made explicit rather than preserving misleading wording:
1. A difference map is empty on a match only if zero-valued entries are removed.
2. Replacement validity compares the number of required replacements with the available budget.
3. Matrix simulation compares a visited count (or answer.length), not an array object, with the total number of cells. The rotation identity specifically describes 90° clockwise.
The prefix-frequency seed note specifies processing nonempty prefixes: if you explicitly process the empty prefix yourself, do not count it twice.
The tree covers the full previously proposed study map, with 150 distinct primary problem assignments. It is not an enumeration of every algorithmic topic in existence.
